card.text: Explore 2008 EV5 in 3D with its published radar shape model.

introduction.text: 2008 EV5 is a small near-Earth asteroid with a radar-derived equatorial ridge interrupted by a large concavity. Explore its original shape and radial heights. The grid marks unavailable surface imagery. The north pole was not covered by the radar images, so its topography and flattening depend on modeling constraints. The pole is uncertain by 10 degrees and equivalent diameter is 400 ± 50 m. The unmodified archive mesh is retained; no resolved optical surface map is supplied.

shape.title: Radar shape model
shape.summary: The shared grid marks unavailable surface imagery on this radar model. The north pole was not covered by the radar images, so its topography and flattening depend on modeling constraints. The pole is uncertain by 10 degrees and equivalent diameter is 400 ± 50 m. The unmodified archive mesh is retained; no resolved optical surface map is supplied. Lighting uses the published pole and arbitrary display phase.

elevation.title: Shape-derived radial height
elevation.summary: False color shows radius at the nearest source-surface point minus a 0.2 km reference sphere. It includes global shape, not gravitational height or independent measured topography. Correspondence farther than 5 m is withheld. The north pole was not covered by the radar images, so its topography and flattening depend on modeling constraints. The pole is uncertain by 10 degrees and equivalent diameter is 400 ± 50 m. The unmodified archive mesh is retained; no resolved optical surface map is supplied.
